paragraphs.text: Swimming outdoors in winter has grown from a hobby of a few enthusiasts into a popular social activity. In one coastal town, a club that started with six members in 2015 now has more than 400.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Members often say that a swim in cold water improves their mood for the rest of the day. Scientists believe this may be linked to the release of hormones when the body is suddenly cooled, although most studies so far have been small.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The activity is not without risk. The shock of entering very cold water causes rapid breathing, which can lead to panic, and swimmers who stay in too long may lose strength in their arms and legs. Clubs therefore advise newcomers to enter the water slowly and to swim close to the shore.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: After leaving the water, swimmers should dress quickly and have a warm drink, but doctors warn against taking a hot shower straight away, because a sudden change in temperature can make some people feel faint.
paragraphs.label: D
